additions.reason: Feelings getting across to another person is a separate sense from 'to be handed down' (traditions) and 'to spread' (news). The ZH list already carries it via 传达; only the English is missing it — the same pattern as most earlier accepted gaps. Transitivity checked: 'to be conveyed' is intransitive, so it does not smuggle in 伝える.

Calling on residents to act is the 'appeal for, call for' sense, distinct from physically calling out to a person, which is all the English offers ('to call out to, to address'). The ZH list already carries it as 呼吁 — English-only gap. A poster cannot 'call out to' anyone, so the current EN line genuinely misleads here.

安易に判断する is the 'easygoing, thoughtless, done without due consideration' sense, a standard second sense that 'easy, simple' does not reach — a learner would read the sentence as 'do not judge easily' and miss the criticism. ZH 轻易的 partly hints at it, but neither list states the pejorative sense outright; this is the strongest gap in the batch.

なにしろ〜ので here is the emphatic-reason use ("what with it being my first time"), not the discourse-shift "anyhow". The ZH line is actively misleading: 无论如何是第一次 is not Chinese, while the evidence needs 毕竟. Unlike most items, the gap is on the Chinese side as well as the English.

Disease sense: インフルエンザが流行っている is "is going around", and a learner applying "to flourish, to be popular" reads "influenza is popular", which is wrong in English. Dictionaries split this from the fashion sense. Note the Chinese list already reaches it — 流行 covers 流感流行 — so this is really an English-side gap, the same pattern as most earlier accepted items.

Every current gloss is adjectival ("specific, particular, designated" / 特定, 指定). 原因を特定する means to pinpoint/determine the cause — a learner reading "specific; particular; designated" beside it gets no verb sense at all, and ZH 指定 means 'designate', not 'identify', so the Chinese list does not cover it either. Same shape as the accepted 単位 case: a real second dictionary sense, not a POS restatement.

The only English gloss is "shadow" — the dark silhouette an object casts (that is 影). 木の日陰で休んだ is the sheltered-from-the-sun spot you sit in, which English calls shade, a separate word a learner cannot derive from "shadow". Same shape as 針 glossed "needle, pin" against clock hands. Note: the Chinese list already carries it (阴凉处 is exactly "shade"), so in practice only the English needs the addition. Not a homophone case — ひかげ 日影 means sunlight, the opposite, and this proposal clearly belongs to 日陰.
